formalDefinition: SUDOKU = {C | C ⊆ {0,…,8} × {0,…,8} × {1,…,9}, and there exists a 9×9 grid H satisfying: (1) ∀(x,y,z) ∈ C, H[x,y] = z; (2) each row contains each value 1…9 exactly once; (3) each column contains each value 1…9 exactly once; (4) each 3×3 block contains each value 1…9 exactly once }
problemDefinition: Sudoku is a logic-based, combinatorial number-placement puzzle where the goal is to fill a 9x9 grid with digits so that each column, row, and 3x3 box contains all of the digits from 1 to 9.
inputDescription: A partially filled 9x9 Sudoku grid of clues
outputDescription: The fully solved 9x9 grid (9 rows of 9 digits 1-9, rows separated by semicolons) that matches every clue, or {} if the clues admit no solution
source: Bhattarai, Apekshya, Dinisha Uprety, Pooja Pathak, Safal Shrestha, Salina Narkarmi, and Sanjog Sigdel. 2025. “A Study of Sudoku Solving Algorithms: Backtracking and Heuristic.” Department of Computer Science, Kathmandu University.
certificateFormat: Format: same 9-rows-of-9 semicolon-separated digit format, fully filled (no zeros): each row, column, and 3x3 block has 1-9 exactly once, matching every instance clue Example: 6,4,8,1,9,5,2,7,3;3,2,1,7,4,8,5,9,6;9,7,5,3,2,6,4,8,1;5,9,2,6,7,1,8,3,4;8,6,7,4,3,2,1,5,9;1,3,4,8,5,9,6,2,7;2,1,9,5,6,3,7,4,8;7,5,6,9,8,4,3,1,2;4,8,3,2,1,7,9,6,5

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a verifier for Sudoku. It takes the certificate from the user and validates that it follows the rules of Sudoku and matches the initial clues from the problem instance.

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: Draws the 9 x 9 grid as a table, rows and columns numbered from 1. The clues stand as given; once solved, every square the solver filled in is shown in the Solution color.
